content:
support-liaison: FYI we have a customer-facing escalation — multiple customers seeing 502/500 from the API when they should be getting 429 for quota rejections. Customer reports started ~09:12 UTC. High priority.

elaine: Which endpoint and any repro steps? Are they getting 5xx consistently or intermittent?

support-liaison: Endpoint: POST /v1/generate (hosted). Example customer cID=acme-123. They get 502 with body: `{\n  \"error\": \"quota service returned internal error\"\n}`. Happening across regions us-west-2 and eu-west-1 intermittently.

miguel: I grabbed a quick repro from a dev account. Reproducer curl:```\ncurl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXXX' \\n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n  -d '{"model":"rw1-large","input":"hello","client_id":"acme-123"}'\n```\nWhen quota path trips it returns 502. Raw response headers include `x-service-quota: quota-orch` and `x-upstream-status: 504`. Full response:```\nHTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway\nContent-Type: application/json\n\n{\"error\":\"quota-orch->token-service timeout (504)\"}```

jess: I pulled logs from quota-orch for the time window. Relevant lines:```\n[2026-03-14T09:12:21Z] quota-orch request id=abc123 client=acme-123 decision=DENY backend=kvs timeout=1200ms err=upstream timeout\n[2026-03-14T09:12:21Z] quota-orch returning 502 for decision=DENY code=internal_error\n[2026-03-14T09:12:21Z] upstream token-service error: context deadline exceeded\n```\nThis looks like quota-orch treating dependency timeouts as internal errors and returning 5xx instead of mapping deny -> 4xx.

oncall-mike: We saw similar pattern in last week's deploy where token-service had transient latency after a config change. Possible misroute: quota-orch's fallback policy marks requests as internal when kvstore or token-service times out. Short-term mitigation: convert quota-orch 5xx -> 429 at the gateway layer for known error shapes. I can flip a proxy rule.

ops-bot: deploy request queued: set-route-mapping:api-proxy convert-quota-5xx->429 (dry-run) by oncall-mike.

eng-sre-bot: Alert rule fired: quota-orch 5xx rate increased by 7x in the last 10m; p50 latency token-service increased from 35ms -> 1.4s.

miguel: Repro steps for logs collection:```\n# kubectl logs -n prod -l app=quota-orch --since=30m | grep \"DENY\" -A3\n# honeycomb query: service=quota-orch filter=status>=500 group_by=error_message\n```\nAlso captured request/response example in request-id=abc123.

elaine: For customer comms we need: root cause summary, mitigation, ETA for permanent fix, and guidance for customers (workarounds). I'll draft a short blurb but need concrete temp mitigation.

oncall-mike: Temporary fix applied: API proxy rule enabled that maps responses matching `quota-orch.*timeout` or `x-upstream-status: 504` -> 429 with body `{"error":"quota_exceeded"}` for affected clients (route-level). This is behind a feature flag and scoped to customer tier 'standard' only. Patch ID: pf-20260314-01. Rolling in canary (10%): ops-bot shows: canary deploy started.

jess: Quick note on correctness — we should only map when decision==DENY. If it's truly an internal error (eg storage corruption) mapping to 429 would hide legitimate 5xx and potentially mask real outages. Logs show decision=DENY in most cases, but we need to be conservative.

miguel: Agreed. From payload samples majority have `decision=DENY` and `err=upstream timeout`. Looks like quota-orch is enforcing but then failing to surface a 4xx because its dependency timed out while computing tokens. Implementation bug: quota-orch default path sets status=500 when backend call fails instead of returning a bounded deny.

jess: Proposed long-term fixes: 1) Fix quota-orch to return explicit 429/403 for enforce decisions regardless of dependency latency; 2) Add circuit breaker & local cache for token/kvs lookups so short dependency hiccups don't blow up decisions; 3) Add observability flag to emit `x-quota-decision` header for easier classification at proxy level.

support-liaison: For immediate customer messaging: "We're aware of intermittent 502/500 responses from our API when requests hit quota enforcement. We're applying a mitigation to return quota_exceeded (429) for affected traffic while we fix the enforcement service. No data loss. More updates in 1-2 hours." OK?

elaine: That works. I'll push a status update to the incident page and CS.

oncall-mike: Canary looks healthy at 10% for 15m. No increase in error budgets. Rolling to 50% now. ops-bot: deploy progress 50%.

jess: Created GH issue: redwood/quota-orch#487 with repro, logs, and suggested patch. Assigning to eng-runtime team. Link: https://github.com/redwood/quota-orch/issues/487

miguel: For postmortem items: - owner: eng-runtime (fix return codes + circuit breaker) - owner: eng-platform (proxy header for x-quota-decision) - owner: monitoring (alert on decision==DENY but status>=500) - ETA: hotfix + deploy in next 48h, full design in 1 week.

eng-sre-bot: Incident Severity: Sev3 -> elevated to Sev2 based on customer impact across multiple accounts. Pager rotation notified.

support-liaison: Customers notified via support tickets and status page. Keeping open until quota-orch patch merges and we see 24h stable.

elaine: Thanks everyone — keep updates here. If anyone finds counterexamples (true internal errors being mapped) call it out immediately.

ops-bot: canary deploy pf-20260314-01 -> 100% complete.

jess: Patch merged to main for conservative mapping and 429 guarantee: PR #490. Will schedule rollout with eng-runtime for 02:00 UTC tomorrow.

support-liaison: Marking initial customer comms sent. Will update once patch is live and we've observed 24h stability.

end of thread
